title: Can You Actually Feel Pain in Your Sleep? 😱
hook_text: Your brain blocks pain at night
script: Your brain shuts off pain signals while you sleep — almost completely. During REM sleep, your thalamus stops relaying sensory signals to the cortex. That's your brain's relay station going dark. Researcher Peretz Lavie confirmed in the 1990s that pain thresholds spike by up to 50% during deep sleep — meaning injuries that would wake you cold sober barely register at night. That's why surgeons historically operated on sedated patients and called it mercy. So if pain woke you last night — how bad was it actually? And that's why.
search_summary: During REM sleep the thalamus blocks pain signals raising pain thresholds by 50 percent
